pais.texto:
Australia is a country and a continent at once. It is the home of animals like the kangaroo and the koala.
Before the British arrived in 1788, Aboriginal peoples already spoke hundreds of languages there. Words like kangaroo, boomerang and koala came into English from them.
fatos: English and more than 100 Indigenous languages

lesson.introText: Today, we’ll talk about Australia. We’ll take a look at Aussie English, food, animals and famous places.
lesson.introSub: Aussie English, food, animals and famous places

warmup.question: How well do you know Australia?
modelAnswers: I don’t know a lot about it.
I know a little: kangaroos and koalas!

warmup.question: Would you like to visit Australia?
modelAnswers: Yes, I would. It looks amazing!
No, I wouldn’t. It’s too far.

fotos.local: Uluru, in the centre of Australia
fotos.texto: Uluru is the red monolith in the centre of the country. It is sacred to the Anangu people.
The Great Barrier Reef is the largest coral reef system on the planet.
Bondi is one of the best-known beaches in Sydney, famous for surfing. December is summer in Australia, and many people spend Christmas at the beach!
Vegemite is a dark, very salty spread. Because it is so salty, Australians put only a thin layer on their toast.
A cube of sponge cake covered in chocolate and coconut: a classic Australian sweet.

lesson.vocabSub: words you will hear in Australia · pay attention to pronunciation

conversation.question: Would you like to see a kangaroo or a koala?
modelAnswers: I’d like to see a (koala).
I’d like to see both!

conversation.question: Do you like the beach?
modelAnswers: Yes, I do. I love the beach!
No, I don’t. I prefer the mountains.

conversation.question: Would you like to spend Christmas on the beach, like many Australians?
modelAnswers: Yes, I would. It sounds fun!
No, I wouldn’t. I prefer Christmas at home.

conversation.question: What do you usually eat for brekkie (breakfast)?
modelAnswers: I usually eat (bread and butter).
I usually have (coffee with milk).

conversation.question: Would you like to try Vegemite on toast?
modelAnswers: Yes, I would.
No, I wouldn’t. It’s too salty for me!

conversation.question: What’s your favorite sweet?
modelAnswers: My favorite sweet is (brigadeiro).
I don’t like sweets.

conversation.question: Australians say “mate” to friends and even to strangers. What do you call your friends?
modelAnswers: I call my friends (cara / mano / amiga).

conversation.question: Do you like to shorten words, like “brekkie” for breakfast?
modelAnswers: Yes, I do. I say (“niver”) for (“aniversário”).
No, I don’t.

conversation.question: Do you like barbecues (barbies)?
modelAnswers: Yes, I do. We have barbecues on (Sundays).
No, I don’t.

evaluation.question: Did you enjoy talking about Australia?
Which other countries would you like to learn more about? I’d like to know more about... (Canada).
